text:
jin: rolling out model v3-int8 to canary (1% traffic) now. quick heads-up — small-batch p95 latency is spiking compared to fp16 baseline :thinking_face:

alisha: how big are the spikes? numbers?

jin: short summary: avg latency ~42ms (baseline 35ms), p95 ~210ms (baseline 120ms). cost per token down ~22%. error rate for long-form summarization task up from 1.2% -> 2.8% (rough count from recent evals).

sam: that p95 delta is concerning for interactive flows. are these tied to tiny batch sizes (<4)?

jin: yes, correlates with request sizes. most affected when batch size = 1 or 2. looks like kernel warmup + kv cache path in int8 isn't hitting optimized kernel for short sequences.

maria: can we gate by request-size histogram in the canary policy? E.g. only route requests with batch_size>=4 or expected seq_len>128?

jin: we already have routing rules but current canary is global 1%. we can do route-based split. proposal: restrict int8 canary to non-interactive paths (batch>=4) and leave interactive traffic on fp16 until we confirm micro-latency fixes.

ai-eval-bot: eval report attached ->
- benchmark suite: long-form-summ, qna, chat-short
- long-form-summ: regression +1.6% err (ROUGE-L drop ~0.9)
- qna/chat-short: no meaningful quality drop
- tokenization edgecases: +0.3% failure rate

alisha: OK. what's our automatic fallback trigger? current canary policy has: fallback_if_quality_delta > 0.015 over 10m OR p95 latency increase > 1.5x for 5m.

sam: those numbers would have triggered already (p95 210 vs 120 = 1.75x). why didn't we auto-fallback?

jin: canary traffic has low request volume; metric smoothing and min_samples params prevented eviction. policy has min_requests: 1000 in 15m. our canary only saw ~230 requests in the window.

maria: this is the classic small-sample blind spot. suggestions: 1) add hysteresis that combines relative change + absolute delta, 2) reduce min_requests for small-percentage canaries, 3) add sample-weighted alerts that upweight critical routes.

sam: +1 to sample-weighted. Also consider a 'fast-fail' rule for p95 > 1.6x AND p95_abs > 150ms for any 5m window regardless of sample count. That would catch interactive regressions quickly.

jin: drafting config now. proposed snippet:
```yaml
canary_policy:
  canary_percent: 1.0
  min_requests: 250             # lowered from 1000
  metrics:
    - name: p95_latency
      relative_threshold: 1.6
      absolute_threshold_ms: 150
      window: 5m
      fast_fail: true
    - name: quality_delta
      threshold: 0.015
      window: 10m
      smoothing: moving_avg_3
  hysteresis:
    require_consecutive_violations: 2
    decay_minutes: 30
```

ai-eval-bot: additional note -> A/B slice shows the long-form regression concentrated on documents > 800 tokens and with many list-like bullet points. Suggest we add targeted eval set and a fallback to fp16 for requests with seq_len>1024 for now.

maria: also propose KL-divergence drift detector for distributional shift vs baseline. if KL>0.12 for 15m, pause canary and flag SRE.

alisha: agree. combined plan: 1) restrict int8 canary to batch>=4 non-interactive routes, 2) lower min_requests to 250, add fast-fail p95 rule, 3) add seq_len-based automatic fallback to fp16 for seq_len>1024, 4) add KL drift monitor. rollback if any of (fast-fail OR quality_delta) triggers.

jin: implementing changes and will re-run a smoke test on staging. staging smoke run shows p95 now ~130ms for batch=1 after a microkernel tweak (still not perfect).

deploy-bot: deploy v3-int8-canary config updated by jin at 1935023476 :rocket:

sam: timeline preference? rollback if triggers within next 2 hours automatically, otherwise evaluate 24h A/B metrics.

maria: I'll wire up the KL detector and a per-route sample-weighted dashboard metric (link: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/canary-int8-quicklook).

jin: thanks. lowering canary to 0.5% and enabling seq_len fallback now. will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
